                    ### Question
                    A 3175-g (7-lb) female newborn is delivered at term. Initial examination shows a distended abdomen and a flat perineal region without an opening. A dark green discharge is coming out of the vulva. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Meconium ileus
opb. Hirschsprung disease
opc. Imperforate anus
opd. Colonic atresia
ope. Meconium plug syndrome
"

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The clinical presentation of a distended abdomen, flat perineal region without an anal opening, and dark green discharge from the vulva strongly suggests an anorectal malformation. The presence of meconium indicates a blockage, which is most consistent with an imperforate anus. This condition is characterized by the absence of a normal anal opening, leading to gastrointestinal obstruction and the accumulation of meconium. The reasoning chains consistently point towards imperforate anus as the most likely diagnosis, supported by the clinical signs observed. Other options like meconium ileus, Hirschsprung disease, colonic atresia, and meconium plug syndrome do not align as closely with the specific findings of this case.
